texts.1pe.2.12: Tendo o vosso viver honesto entre os gentios; para que, n’aquillo em que fallam mal de vós, como de malfeitores, glorifiquem a Deus no dia da visitação, pelas boas obras que em vós virem.
texts.1pe.2.13: Sujeitae-vos pois a toda a ordenação humana por amor do Senhor: seja ao rei, como ao superior;
texts.1pe.2.14: Seja aos governadores, como aos que por elle são enviados para castigo dos malfeitores, e para louvor dos que fazem o bem.
texts.1pe.2.15: Porque assim é a vontade de Deus, que, fazendo bem, tapeis a bocca á ignorancia dos homens loucos:
texts.1pe.2.16: Como libertos, e não como tendo a liberdade por cobertura da malicia, mas como servos de Deus.
texts.1pe.2.17: Honrae a todos. Amae a fraternidade. Temei a Deus. Honrae o rei.
texts.1pe.2.18: Vós, servos, sujeitae-vos com todo o temor aos senhores, não sómente aos bons e humanos, mas tambem aos rigorosos.
texts.1pe.2.19: Porque é coisa agradavel, se alguem, por causa da consciencia para com Deus, soffre aggravos, padecendo injustamente.
texts.1pe.2.20: Porque, que louvor é, se, peccando, sois esbofeteados e soffreis? Mas se, fazendo bem, sois affligidos, e o soffreis, isso é agradavel a Deus.
texts.1pe.2.21: Porque para isto sois chamados; pois tambem Christo padeceu por nós, deixando-nos o exemplo, para que sigaes as suas pisadas.
texts.1pe.2.22: O qual não commetteu peccado, nem na sua bocca se achou engano.
texts.1pe.2.23: O qual, quando o injuriavam, não injuriava, e quando padecia não ameaçava, mas entregava-se áquelle que julga justamente:
texts.1pe.2.24: O qual levou elle mesmo em seu corpo os nossos peccados sobre o madeiro, para que, mortos para os peccados, vivamos para a justiça; por cuja ferida sarastes.
texts.1pe.2.25: Porque ereis como ovelhas desgarradas: mas agora estaes convertidos ao Pastor e Bispo das vossas almas.
texts.1pe.3.1: Similhantemente vós, mulheres, sêde sujeitas aos vossos proprios maridos; para que tambem, se alguns não obedecem á palavra, pelo trato das mulheres sejam ganhos sem palavra;
texts.1pe.3.2: Considerando o vosso casto trato em temor.
texts.1pe.3.3: O enfeite d’ellas não seja o exterior, no encrespamento dos cabellos, ou atavio de oiro, ou compostura de vestidos;
texts.1pe.3.4: Mas o homem encoberto no coração; no incorruptivel de um espirito manso e quieto, que é precioso diante de Deus.
texts.1pe.3.5: Porque assim se enfeitavam tambem antigamente as sanctas mulheres que esperavam em Deus, e estavam sujeitas aos seus proprios maridos;
texts.1pe.3.6: Como Sara obedecia a Abrahão, chamando-lhe senhor; da qual vós sois feitas filhas, fazendo o bem, e não temendo nenhum espanto.
texts.1pe.3.7: Egualmente vós, maridos, cohabitae com ellas com entendimento, dando honra á mulher, como a vaso mais fraco; como aquelles que juntamente com ellas sois herdeiros da graça da vida; para que não sejam impedidas as vossas orações.
texts.1pe.3.8: E, finalmente, sêde todos de um mesmo sentimento, compassivos, amando os irmãos, entranhavelmente misericordiosos e affaveis.
texts.1pe.3.9: Não tornando mal por mal, ou injuria por injuria; antes, pelo contrario, bemdizendo: sabendo que para isto sois chamados, para que por herança alcanceis a benção.
texts.1pe.3.10: Porque quem quer amar a vida, e vêr os dias bons, refreie a sua lingua do mal, e os seus labios que não fallem engano.
texts.1pe.3.11: Aparte-se do mal, e faça o bem; busque a paz, e siga-a.
texts.1pe.3.12: Porque os olhos do Senhor estão sobre os justos, e os seus ouvidos attentos ás suas orações; mas o rosto do Senhor é contra os que fazem males.
texts.1pe.3.13: E qual é aquelle que vos fará mal, se fordes imitadores do bem?
texts.1pe.3.14: Mas tambem, se padecerdes por amor da justiça, sois bemaventurados. E não temaes com medo d’elles, nem vos turbeis;
texts.1pe.3.15: Antes sanctificae o Senhor Deus em vossos corações; e estae sempre preparados para responder com mansidão e temor a qualquer que vos pedir a razão da esperança que ha em vós:
texts.1pe.3.16: Tendo uma boa consciencia, para que, em o que fallam mal de vós, como de malfeitores, fiquem confundidos os que blasphemam do vosso bom trato em Christo.
texts.1pe.3.17: Porque melhor é que padeçaes fazendo bem (se a vontade de Deus assim o quer), do que fazendo mal.
texts.1pe.3.18: Porque tambem Christo padeceu uma vez pelos peccados, o justo pelos injustos, para levar-nos a Deus; mortificado, na verdade, na carne, porém vivificado pelo Espirito;
texts.1pe.3.19: No qual tambem foi, e prégou aos espiritos em prisão;
texts.1pe.3.20: Os quaes antigamente foram rebeldes, quando a longanimidade de Deus esperava nos dias de Noé, apparelhando-se a arca; na qual poucas (isto é oito) almas se salvaram pela agua;
texts.1pe.3.21: Que tambem, como uma verdadeira figura, agora nos salva, o baptismo não o do despojamento da immundicia do corpo, mas o da indagação de uma boa consciencia para com Deus, pela resurreição de Jesus Christo;
texts.1pe.3.22: O qual está á dextra de Deus, tendo subido ao céu: havendo-se-lhe sujeitado os anjos, e as auctoridades, e as potencias.
texts.1pe.4.1: Ora pois, já que Christo padeceu por nós na carne, armae-vos tambem vós com este pensamento, que aquelle que padeceu na carne já cessou do peccado,
texts.1pe.4.2: Para, no tempo que lhe resta na carne, não viver mais segundo as concupiscencias dos homens, mas segundo a vontade de Deus.
texts.1pe.4.3: Porque basta-nos que no tempo passado da vida obrassemos a vontade dos gentios, andando em dissoluções, concupiscencias, borrachices, glotonerias, bebedices e abominaveis idolatrias,
texts.1pe.4.4: O que estranham, por não correrdes com elles no mesmo desenfreamento de dissolução, blasphemando de vós.
texts.1pe.4.5: Os quaes hão de dar conta ao que está preparado para julgar os vivos e os mortos.
texts.1pe.4.6: Porque para isso foi prégado o evangelho tambem aos mortos, para que, na verdade, fossem julgados segundo os homens na carne, porém vivessem segundo Deus em espirito;
texts.1pe.4.7: E já está proximo o fim de todas as coisas: portanto sêde sobrios e vigiae em orações.
texts.1pe.4.8: Mas, sobretudo, tende ardente caridade uns para com os outros; porque a caridade cobrirá a multidão de peccados.
texts.1pe.4.9: Hospedae-vos uns aos outros, sem murmurações.
texts.1pe.4.10: Cada um administre aos outros o dom como o recebeu, como bons dispenseiros da multiforme graça de Deus.
texts.1pe.4.11: Se alguem fallar, falle segundo as palavras de Deus; se alguem administrar, administre segundo o poder que Deus dá; para que em tudo Deus seja glorificado por Jesus Christo, a quem pertence a gloria e poder para todo o sempre. Amen.
texts.1pe.4.12: Amados, não estranheis o ardor que vos sobrevem para vos tentar, como se coisa estranha vos acontecesse;
texts.1pe.4.13: Mas alegrae-vos de serdes participantes das afflicções de Christo: para que tambem na revelação da sua gloria vos regozijeis e alegreis.
texts.1pe.4.14: Se pelo nome de Christo sois vituperados, bemaventurados sois, porque sobre vós repousa o Espirito da gloria de Deus; o qual, quanto a elles, é blasphemado, mas, quanto a vós, glorificado.
texts.1pe.4.15: Porém nenhum de vós padeça como homicida, ou ladrão, ou malfeitor, ou como o que se entremette em negocios alheios;
texts.1pe.4.16: Mas, se padece como christão, não se envergonhe, antes glorifique a Deus n’esta parte.
texts.1pe.4.17: Porque já é tempo que comece o juizo pela casa de Deus; e, se primeiro começa por nós, qual será o fim d’aquelles que são desobedientes ao evangelho de Deus?
texts.1pe.4.18: E, se o justo apenas se salva, onde apparecerá o impio e o peccador?
texts.1pe.4.19: Portanto tambem os que padecem segundo a vontade de Deus encommendem-lhe as suas almas, como ao fiel Creador, fazendo o bem.
texts.1pe.5.1: Aos anciãos, que estão entre vós, admoesto eu, que sou juntamente como elles ancião, e testemunha das afflicções de Christo, e participante da gloria que se ha de revelar.
texts.1pe.5.2: Apascentae o rebanho de Deus, que está entre vós, tendo cuidado d’elle, não por força, mas voluntariamente; nem por torpe ganancia, mas de um animo prompto,
texts.1pe.5.3: Nem como tendo dominio sobre a herança de Deus, mas servindo de exemplo ao rebanho.
texts.1pe.5.4: E, quando apparecer o Summo Pastor, alcançareis a incorruptivel corôa de gloria.
texts.1pe.5.5: Similhantemente vós, mancebos, sêde sujeitos aos anciãos; e sêde todos sujeitos uns aos outros, e vesti-vos de humildade, porque Deus resiste aos soberbos, mas dá graça aos humildes.
texts.1pe.5.6: Humilhae-vos pois debaixo da potente mão de Deus, para que a seu tempo vos exalte:
texts.1pe.5.7: Lançando sobre elle toda a vossa solicitude, porque elle tem cuidado de vós.
texts.1pe.5.8: Sêde sobrios; vigiae; porque o diabo, vosso adversario, anda em derredor, bramando como leão, buscando a quem possa tragar.
texts.1pe.5.9: Ao qual resisti firmes na fé: sabendo que as mesmas afflicções se cumprem entre os vossos irmãos no mundo.
texts.1pe.5.10: Ora o Deus de toda a graça, que em Christo Jesus nos chamou á sua eterna gloria, depois de haverdes padecido um pouco, o mesmo vos aperfeiçoe, confirme, fortifique e estabeleça.
texts.1pe.5.11: A elle seja a gloria e o poderio para todo o sempre. Amen.
texts.1pe.5.12: Por Silvano, vosso fiel irmão, como cuido, escrevi abreviadamente, exhortando e testificando que esta é a verdadeira graça de Deus, na qual estaes.
texts.1pe.5.13: Sauda-vos a egreja co-eleita, que está em Babylonia, e meu filho Marcos.
texts.1pe.5.14: Saudae-vos uns aos outros com osculo de caridade. Paz seja com todos vós que estaes em Christo Jesus. Amen.

texts.1pe.1.1: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,
texts.1pe.1.2: Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, through sanctification of the Spirit, to obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: Grace to you, and peace, be multiplied.
texts.1pe.1.3: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his abundant mercy hath begotten us again to a living hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
texts.1pe.1.4: To an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for you,
texts.1pe.1.5: Who are kept by the power of God through faith to salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.
texts.1pe.1.6: In which ye greatly rejoice, though now for a season (if need be) ye are in heaviness through manifold temptations:
texts.1pe.1.7: That the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though tried with fire, might be found to praise, and honor, and glory, at the appearing of Jesus Christ:
texts.1pe.1.8: Whom having not seen, ye love; in whom, though now ye see him not, yet believing, ye rejoice with joy unspeakable, and full of glory:
texts.1pe.1.9: Receiving the end of your faith, even the salvation of your souls.
texts.1pe.1.10: Concerning which salvation the prophets have inquired and searched diligently, who prophesied of the grace that should come to you:
texts.1pe.1.11: Searching what, or what manner of time the Spirit of Christ which was in them did signify, when it testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that should follow.
texts.1pe.1.12: To whom it was revealed, that not to themselves, but to us they ministered the things which are now reported to you by them that have preached the gospel to you, with the Holy Spirit sent down from heaven; which things the angels desire to look into.
texts.1pe.1.13: Wherefore gird up the loins of your mind, be sober, and hope to the end for the grace that is to be brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ;
texts.1pe.1.14: As obedient children, not fashioning yourselves according to the former lusts in your ignorance:
texts.1pe.1.15: But as he who hath called you is holy, so be ye holy in all manner of deportment.
texts.1pe.1.16: Because it is written, Be ye holy; for I am holy.
texts.1pe.1.17: And if ye call on the Father, who without respect of persons judgeth according to every man's work, pass the time of your sojourning here in fear:
texts.1pe.1.18: Forasmuch as ye know that ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold, from your vain course of life received by tradition from your fathers;
texts.1pe.1.19: But with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot:
texts.1pe.1.20: Who verily was fore-ordained before the foundation of the world, but was manifested in these last times for you,
texts.1pe.1.21: Who by him do believe in God, that raised him from the dead, and gave him glory; that your faith and hope might be in God.
texts.1pe.1.22: Seeing ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit to unfeigned love of the brethren, see that ye love one another with a pure heart fervently:
texts.1pe.1.23: Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.
texts.1pe.1.24: For all flesh is as grass, and all the glory of man as the flower of grass. The grass withereth, and its flower falleth away:
texts.1pe.1.25: But the word of the Lord endureth for ever. And this is the word which by the gospel is preached to you.
texts.1pe.2.1: Wherefore, laying aside all malice, and all guile, and hypocrisies, and envies, and all evil-speakings,
texts.1pe.2.2: As new-born babes, desire the pure milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby:
texts.1pe.2.3: If indeed ye have tasted that the Lord is gracious.
texts.1pe.2.4: To whom coming as to a living stone, disallowed indeed by men, but chosen by God, and precious,
texts.1pe.2.5: Ye also, as living stones, are built up a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ.
texts.1pe.2.6: Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner-stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded.
texts.1pe.2.7: To you therefore who believe he is precious: but to them who are disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner,
texts.1pe.2.8: And a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offense, even to them who stumble at the word, being disobedient: to which also they were appointed.
texts.1pe.2.9: But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should show forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvelous light:
texts.1pe.2.10: Who in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: who had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.
texts.1pe.2.11: Dearly beloved, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul;
texts.1pe.2.12: Having your manner of life honest among the Gentiles: that, whereas they speak against you as evil-doers, they may by your good works, which they shall behold, glorify God in the day of visitation.
texts.1pe.2.13: Submit yourselves to every ordinance of man for the Lord's sake: whether to the king, as supreme;
texts.1pe.2.14: Or to governors, as to them that are sent by him for the punishment of evil-doers, and for the praise of them that do well.
texts.1pe.2.15: For so is the will of God, that with well-doing ye may put to silence the ignorance of foolish men:
texts.1pe.2.16: As free, and not using your liberty for a cloke of maliciousness, but as the servants of God.
texts.1pe.2.17: Honor all men. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honor the king.
texts.1pe.2.18: Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear; not only to the good and gentle, but also to the froward.
texts.1pe.2.19: For this is thank-worthy, if a man for conscience towards God endureth grief, suffering wrongfully.
texts.1pe.2.20: For what glory is it, if, when ye are buffeted for your faults, ye bear it patiently? but if, when ye do well, and suffer for it, ye bear it patiently, this is acceptable with God.
texts.1pe.2.21: For even to this were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps:
texts.1pe.2.22: Who committed no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth:
texts.1pe.2.23: Who, when he was reviled, reviled not again; when he suffered, he threatened not; but committed himself to him that judgeth righteously:
texts.1pe.2.24: Who himself bore our sins in his own body on the tree, that we, being dead to sins, should live to righteousness; by whose stripes ye were healed.
texts.1pe.2.25: For ye were as sheep going astray; but are now returned to the Shepherd and Bishop of your souls.
texts.1pe.3.1: Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the deportment of the wives;
texts.1pe.3.2: While they behold your chaste manner of life coupled with fear.
texts.1pe.3.3: Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing gold, or of putting on apparel;
texts.1pe.3.4: But let it be the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price.
texts.1pe.3.5: For after this manner in former times the holy women also, who trusted in God, adorned themselves, being in subjection to their own husbands:
texts.1pe.3.6: Even as Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement.
texts.1pe.3.7: Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honor to the wife, as to the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered.
texts.1pe.3.8: Finally, be ye all of one mind, having compassion one of another; love as brethren, be pitiful, be courteous:
texts.1pe.3.9: Not rendering evil for evil, or railing for railing: but on the contrary, blessing; knowing that ye are called to this, that ye should inherit a blessing.
texts.1pe.3.10: For he that will love life, and see good days, let him restrain his tongue from evil, and his lips that they speak no guile:
texts.1pe.3.11: Let him shun evil, and do good; let him seek peace, and pursue it.
texts.1pe.3.12: For the eyes of the Lord are over the righteous, and his ears are open to their prayers: but the face of the Lord is against them that do evil.
texts.1pe.3.13: And who is he that will harm you, if ye are followers of that which is good?
texts.1pe.3.14: But if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled;
texts.1pe.3.15: But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you, with meekness and fear.
texts.1pe.3.16: Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evil-doers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good deportment in Christ.
texts.1pe.3.17: For it is better, if the will of God is so, that ye suffer for well-doing, than for evil-doing.
texts.1pe.3.18: For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh, but made alive by the Spirit:
texts.1pe.3.19: By which also he went and preached to the spirits in prison;
texts.1pe.3.20: Who formerly were disobedient, when once the long-suffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was preparing, in which few, that is, eight souls, were saved by water.
texts.1pe.3.21: The like figure to which, even baptism, doth also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience towards God,) by the resurrection of Jesus Christ:
texts.1pe.3.22: Who is gone into heaven, and is on the right hand of God; angels, and authorities, and powers being made subject to him.
texts.1pe.4.1: Forasmuch then as Christ hath suffered for us in the flesh, arm yourselves likewise with the same mind: for he that hath suffered in the flesh hath ceased from sin;
texts.1pe.4.2: That he no longer should live the rest of his time in the flesh to the lusts of men, but to the will of God.
texts.1pe.4.3: For the time past of our life may suffice us to have wrought the will of the Gentiles, when we walked in lasciviousness, lusts, excess of wine, revelings, banquetings, and abominable idolatries:
texts.1pe.4.4: In which they think it strange that ye run not with them to the same excess of riot, speaking evil of you:
texts.1pe.4.5: Who shall give account to him that is ready to judge the living and the dead.
texts.1pe.4.6: For, for this cause was the gospel preached also to them that are dead, that they might be judged according to men in the flesh, but live according to God in the spirit.
texts.1pe.4.7: But the end of all things is at hand: be ye therefore sober, and watch to prayer.
texts.1pe.4.8: And above all things have fervent charity among yourselves: for charity will cover a multitude of sins.
texts.1pe.4.9: Use hospitality one to another without grudging.
texts.1pe.4.10: As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.
texts.1pe.4.11: If any man speaketh let him speak as the oracles of God; if any man ministereth let him do it as of the ability which God giveth: that God in all things may be glorified through Jesus Christ; to whom be praise and dominion for ever and ever. Amen.
texts.1pe.4.12: Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened to you:
texts.1pe.4.13: But rejoice, seeing ye are partakers of Christ's sufferings; that, when his glory shall be revealed, ye may be glad also with exceeding joy.
texts.1pe.4.14: If ye are reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye; for the spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you. On their part he is evil spoken of, but on your part he is glorified.
texts.1pe.4.15: But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or as a thief, or as an evil-doer, or as a busy-body in other men's matters.
texts.1pe.4.16: Yet if any man suffereth as a Christian, let him not be ashamed; but let him glorify God on this behalf.
texts.1pe.4.17: For the time is come that judgment must begin at the house of God: and if it first beginneth at us, what will be the end of them that obey not the gospel of God?
texts.1pe.4.18: And if the righteous is scarcely saved, where will the ungodly and the sinner appear?
texts.1pe.4.19: Wherefore, let them that suffer according to the will of God, commit the keeping of their souls to him in well-doing, as to a faithful Creator.
texts.1pe.5.1: The elders who are among you I exhort, who am also an elder, and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and also a partaker of the glory that shall be revealed:
texts.1pe.5.2: Feed the flock of God which is among you, taking the oversight of it, not by constraint, but willingly; not for filthy lucre, but from a ready mind;
texts.1pe.5.3: Neither as being lords over God's heritage, but being examples to the flock.
texts.1pe.5.4: And when the chief Shepherd shall appear, ye shall receive a crown of glory that fadeth not away.
texts.1pe.5.5: Likewise, ye younger, submit yourselves to the elder. Yes, all of you be subject one to another, and be clothed with humility: for God resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble.
texts.1pe.5.6: Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time:
texts.1pe.5.7: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
texts.1pe.5.8: Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour:
texts.1pe.5.9: Whom resist steadfast in the faith, knowing that the same afflictions are accomplished in your brethren that are in the world.
texts.1pe.5.10: But the God of all grace, who hath called us to his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after ye have suffered a while, make you perfect, establish, strengthen, settle you.
texts.1pe.5.11: To him be glory and dominion for ever and ever. Amen.
texts.1pe.5.12: By Silvanus, a faithful brother to you, as I suppose, I have written briefly, exhorting, and testifying that this is the true grace of God in which ye stand.
texts.1pe.5.13: The church that is at Babylon, elected together with you, saluteth you; and so doth Mark my son.
texts.1pe.5.14: Greet ye one another with a kiss of charity. Peace be with you all that are in Christ Jesus. Amen.

texts.1pe.1.1: Peter, apostle of Jesus Christ, to [the] sojourners of [the] dispersion of Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,
texts.1pe.1.2: elect according to [the] foreknowledge of God [the] Father, by sanctification of [the] Spirit, unto [the] obedience and sprinkling of [the] blood of Jesus Christ: Grace to you and peace be multiplied.
texts.1pe.1.3: Blessed [be] the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who, according to his great mercy, has begotten us again to a living hope through [the] resurrection of Jesus Christ from among [the] dead,
texts.1pe.1.4: to an incorruptible and undefiled and unfading inheritance, reserved in [the] heavens for you,
texts.1pe.1.5: who are kept guarded by [the] power of God through faith for salvation ready to be revealed in [the] last time.
texts.1pe.1.6: Wherein ye exult, for a little while at present, if needed, put to grief by various trials,
texts.1pe.1.7: that the proving of your faith, much more precious than of gold which perishes, though it be proved by fire, be found to praise and glory and honour in [the] revelation of Jesus Christ:
texts.1pe.1.8: whom, having not seen, ye love; on whom [though] not now looking, but believing, ye exult with joy unspeakable and filled with [the] glory,
texts.1pe.1.9: receiving the end of your faith, [the] salvation of [your] souls.
texts.1pe.1.10: Concerning which salvation prophets, who have prophesied of the grace towards you, sought out and searched out;
texts.1pe.1.11: searching what, or what manner of time, the Spirit of Christ which [was] in them pointed out, testifying before of the sufferings which [belonged] to Christ, and the glories after these.
texts.1pe.1.12: To whom it was revealed, that not to themselves but to you they ministered those things, which have now been announced to you by those who have declared to you the glad tidings by [the] Holy Spirit, sent from heaven, which angels desire to look into.
texts.1pe.1.13: Wherefore, having girded up the loins of your mind, [be] sober [and] hope with perfect stedfastness in the grace [which will be] brought to you at [the] revelation of Jesus Christ;
texts.1pe.1.14: as children of obedience, not conformed to [your] former lusts in your ignorance;
texts.1pe.1.15: but as he who has called you is holy, be ye also holy in all [your] conversation;
texts.1pe.1.16: because it is written, Be ye holy, for *I* am holy.
texts.1pe.1.17: And if ye invoke as Father him who, without regard of persons, judges according to the work of each, pass your time of sojourn in fear,
texts.1pe.1.18: knowing that ye have been redeemed, not by corruptible [things, as] silver or gold, from your vain conversation handed down from [your] fathers,
texts.1pe.1.19: but by precious blood, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot, [the blood] of Christ,
texts.1pe.1.20: foreknown indeed before [the] foundation of [the] world, but who has been manifested at the end of times for your sakes,
texts.1pe.1.21: who by him do believe on God, who has raised him from among [the] dead and given him glory, that your faith and hope should be in God.
texts.1pe.1.22: Having purified your souls by obedience to the truth to unfeigned brotherly love, love one another out of a pure heart fervently;
texts.1pe.1.23: being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by [the] living and abiding word of God.
texts.1pe.1.24: Because all flesh [is] as grass, and all its glory as [the] flower of grass. The grass has withered and [its] flower has fallen;
texts.1pe.1.25: but the word of [the] Lord abides for eternity. But this is the word which in the glad tidings [is] preached to you.
texts.1pe.2.1: Laying aside therefore all malice and all guile and hypocrisies and envyings and all evil speakings,
texts.1pe.2.2: as newborn babes desire earnestly the pure mental milk of the word, that by it ye may grow up to salvation,
texts.1pe.2.3: if indeed ye have tasted that the Lord [is] good.
texts.1pe.2.4: To whom coming, a living stone, cast away indeed as worthless by men, but with God chosen, precious,
texts.1pe.2.5: yourselves also, as living stones, are being built up a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God by Jesus Christ.
texts.1pe.2.6: Because it is contained in the scripture: Behold, I lay in Zion a corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believes on him shall not be put to shame.
texts.1pe.2.7: To you therefore who believe [is] the preciousness; but to the disobedient, the stone which the builders cast away as worthless, this is become head of [the] corner,
texts.1pe.2.8: and a stone of stumbling and rock of offence; [who] stumble at the word, being disobedient to which also they have been appointed.
texts.1pe.2.9: But *ye* [are] a chosen race, a kingly priesthood, a holy nation, a people for a possession, that ye might set forth the excellencies of him who has called you out of darkness to his wonderful light;
texts.1pe.2.10: who once [were] not a people, but now God's people; who were not enjoying mercy, but now have found mercy.
texts.1pe.2.11: Beloved, I exhort [you], as strangers and sojourners, to abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul;
texts.1pe.2.12: having your conversation honest among the Gentiles, that [as to that] in which they speak against you as evildoers, they may through [your] good works, [themselves] witnessing [them], glorify God in [the] day of visitation.
texts.1pe.2.13: Be in subjection [therefore] to every human institution for the Lord's sake; whether to [the] king as supreme,
texts.1pe.2.14: or to rulers as sent by him, for vengeance on evildoers, and praise to them that do well.
texts.1pe.2.15: Because so is the will of God, that by well-doing ye put to silence the ignorance of senseless men;
texts.1pe.2.16: as free, and not as having liberty as a cloak of malice, but as God's bondmen.
texts.1pe.2.17: Shew honour to all, love the brotherhood, fear God, honour the king.
texts.1pe.2.18: Servants, [be] subject with all fear to your masters, not only to the good and gentle, but also to the ill-tempered.
texts.1pe.2.19: For this [is] acceptable, if one, for conscience sake towards God, endure griefs, suffering unjustly.
texts.1pe.2.20: For what glory [is it], if sinning and being buffeted ye shall bear [it]? but if, doing good and suffering, ye shall bear [it], this is acceptable with God.
texts.1pe.2.21: For to this have ye been called; for Christ also has suffered for you, leaving you a model that ye should follow in his steps:
texts.1pe.2.22: who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth;
texts.1pe.2.23: who, [when] reviled, reviled not again; [when] suffering, threatened not; but gave [himself] over into the hands of him who judges righteously;
texts.1pe.2.24: who himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, in order that, being dead to sins, we may live to righteousness: by whose stripes ye have been healed.
texts.1pe.2.25: For ye were going astray as sheep, but have now returned to the shepherd and overseer of your souls.
texts.1pe.3.1: Likewise, wives, [be] subject to your own husbands, that, even if any are disobedient to the word, they may be gained without [the] word by the conversation of the wives,
texts.1pe.3.2: having witnessed your pure conversation [carried out] in fear;
texts.1pe.3.3: whose adorning let it not be that outward one of tressing of hair, and wearing gold, or putting on apparel;
texts.1pe.3.4: but the hidden man of the heart, in the incorruptible [ornament] of a meek and quiet spirit, which in the sight of God is of great price.
texts.1pe.3.5: For thus also the holy women who have hoped in God heretofore adorned themselves, being subject to their own husbands;
texts.1pe.3.6: as Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord; whose children ye have become, doing good, and not fearing with any kind of consternation.
texts.1pe.3.7: [Ye] husbands likewise, dwell with [them] according to knowledge, as with a weaker, [even] the female, vessel, giving [them] honour, as also fellow-heirs of [the] grace of life, that your prayers be not hindered.
texts.1pe.3.8: Finally, [be] all of one mind, sympathising, full of brotherly love, tender hearted, humble minded;
texts.1pe.3.9: not rendering evil for evil, or railing for railing; but on the contrary, blessing [others], because ye have been called to this, that ye should inherit blessing.
texts.1pe.3.10: For he that will love life and see good days, let him cause his tongue to cease from evil and his lips that they speak no guile.
texts.1pe.3.11: And let him avoid evil, and do good; let him seek peace and pursue it;
texts.1pe.3.12: because [the] eyes of [the] Lord [are] on [the] righteous, and his ears towards their supplications; but [the] face of [the] Lord [is] against them that do evil.
texts.1pe.3.13: And who shall injure you if ye have become imitators of that which [is] good?
texts.1pe.3.14: But if also ye should suffer for righteousness' sake, blessed [are ye]; but be not afraid of their fear, neither be troubled;
texts.1pe.3.15: but sanctify [the] Lord the Christ in your hearts, and [be] always prepared to [give] an answer [to] every one that asks you to give an account of the hope that [is] in you, but with meekness and fear;
texts.1pe.3.16: having a good conscience, that [as to that] in which they speak against you as evildoers, they may be ashamed who calumniate your good conversation in Christ.
texts.1pe.3.17: For [it is] better, if the will of God should will it, to suffer [as] well-doers than [as] evildoers;
texts.1pe.3.18: for Christ indeed has once suffered for sins, [the] just for [the] unjust, that he might bring us to God; being put to death in flesh, but made alive in [the] Spirit,
texts.1pe.3.19: in which also going he preached to the spirits [which are] in prison,
texts.1pe.3.20: heretofore disobedient, when the longsuffering of God waited in [the] days of Noah while the ark was preparing, into which few, that is, eight souls, were saved through water:
texts.1pe.3.21: which figure also now saves you, [even] baptism, not a putting away of [the] filth of flesh, but [the] demand as before God of a good conscience, by [the] resurrection of Jesus Christ,
texts.1pe.3.22: who is at [the] right hand of God, gone into heaven, angels and authorities and powers being subjected to him.
texts.1pe.4.1: Christ, then, having suffered for us in [the] flesh, do *ye* also arm yourselves with the same mind; for he that has suffered in [the] flesh has done with sin,
texts.1pe.4.2: no longer to live the rest of [his] time in [the] flesh to men's lusts, but to God's will.
texts.1pe.4.3: For the time past [is] sufficient [for us] to have wrought the will of the Gentiles, walking in lasciviousness, lusts, wine-drinking, revels, drinkings, and unhallowed idolatries.
texts.1pe.4.4: Wherein they think it strange that ye run not with [them] to the same sink of corruption, speaking injuriously [of you];
texts.1pe.4.5: who shall render account to him who is ready to judge [the] living and [the] dead.
texts.1pe.4.6: For to this [end] were the glad tidings preached to [the] dead also, that they might be judged, as regards men, after [the] flesh, but live, as regards God, after [the] Spirit.
texts.1pe.4.7: But the end of all things is drawn nigh: be sober therefore, and be watchful unto prayers;
texts.1pe.4.8: but before all things having fervent love among yourselves, because love covers a multitude of sins;
texts.1pe.4.9: hospitable one to another, without murmuring;
texts.1pe.4.10: each according as he has received a gift, ministering it to one another, as good stewards of [the] various grace of God.
texts.1pe.4.11: If any one speak -- as oracles of God; if any one minister -- as of strength which God supplies; that God in all things may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom is the glory and the might for the ages of ages. Amen.
texts.1pe.4.12: Beloved, take not [as] strange the fire [of persecution] which has taken place amongst you for [your] trial, as if a strange thing was happening to you;
texts.1pe.4.13: but as ye have share in the sufferings of Christ, rejoice, that in the revelation of his glory also ye may rejoice with exultation.
texts.1pe.4.14: If ye are reproached in [the] name of Christ, blessed [are ye]; for the [Spirit] of glory and the Spirit of God rests upon you: [on their part he is blasphemed, but on your part he is glorified.]
texts.1pe.4.15: Let none of you suffer indeed as murderer, or thief, or evildoer, or as overseer of other people's matters;
texts.1pe.4.16: but if as a christian, let him not be ashamed, but glorify God in this name.
texts.1pe.4.17: For the time of having the judgment begin from the house of God [is come]; but if first from us, what [shall be] the end of those who obey not the glad tidings of God?
texts.1pe.4.18: And if the righteous is difficultly saved, where shall the impious and [the] sinner appear?
texts.1pe.4.19: Wherefore also let them who suffer according to the will of God commit their souls in well-doing to a faithful Creator.
texts.1pe.5.1: The elders which [are] among you I exhort, who [am their] fellow-elder and witness of the sufferings of the Christ, who also [am] partaker of the glory about to be revealed:
texts.1pe.5.2: shepherd the flock of God which [is] among you, exercising oversight, not by necessity, but willingly; not for base gain, but readily;
texts.1pe.5.3: not as lording it over your possessions, but being models for the flock.
texts.1pe.5.4: And when the chief shepherd is manifested ye shall receive the unfading crown of glory.
texts.1pe.5.5: Likewise [ye] younger, be subject to [the] elder, and all of you bind on humility towards one another; for God sets himself against [the] proud, but to [the] humble gives grace.
texts.1pe.5.6: Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in [the due] time;
texts.1pe.5.7: having cast all your care upon him, for he cares about you.
texts.1pe.5.8: Be vigilant, watch. Your adversary [the] devil as a roaring lion walks about seeking whom he may devour.
texts.1pe.5.9: Whom resist, stedfast in faith, knowing that the selfsame sufferings are accomplished in your brotherhood which [is] in [the] world.
texts.1pe.5.10: But the God of all grace who has called you to his eternal glory in Christ Jesus, when ye have suffered for a little while, himself shall make perfect, stablish, strengthen, ground:
texts.1pe.5.11: to him [be] the glory and the might for the ages of the ages. Amen.
texts.1pe.5.12: By Silvanus, the faithful brother, as I suppose, I have written to you briefly; exhorting and testifying that this is [the] true grace of God in which ye stand.
texts.1pe.5.13: She that is elected with [you] in Babylon salutes you, and Marcus my son.
texts.1pe.5.14: Salute one another with a kiss of love. Peace be with you all who [are] in Christ.

texts.1pe.1.1: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the choice sojourners of the dispersion of Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,
texts.1pe.1.2: according to a foreknowledge of God the Father, in sanctification of the Spirit, to obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: Grace to you and peace be multiplied!
texts.1pe.1.3: Blessed [is] the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who, according to the abundance of His kindness did beget us again to a living hope, through the rising again of Jesus Christ out of the dead,
texts.1pe.1.4: to an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and unfading, reserved in the heavens for you,
texts.1pe.1.5: who, in the power of God are being guarded, through faith, unto salvation, ready to be revealed in the last time,
texts.1pe.1.6: in which ye are glad, a little now, if it be necessary, being made to sorrow in manifold trials,
texts.1pe.1.7: that the proof of your faith -- much more precious than of gold that is perishing, and through fire being approved -- may be found to praise, and honour, and glory, in the revelation of Jesus Christ,
texts.1pe.1.8: whom, not having seen, ye love, in whom, now not seeing and believing, ye are glad with joy unspeakable and glorified,
texts.1pe.1.9: receiving the end of your faith -- salvation of souls;
texts.1pe.1.10: concerning which salvation seek out and search out did prophets who concerning the grace toward you did prophecy,
texts.1pe.1.11: searching in regard to what or what manner of time the Spirit of Christ that was in them was manifesting, testifying beforehand the sufferings of Christ and the glory after these,
texts.1pe.1.12: to whom it was revealed, that not to themselves, but to us they were ministering these, which now were told to you (through those who did proclaim good news to you,) in the Holy Spirit sent from heaven, to which things messengers do desire to bend looking.
texts.1pe.1.13: Wherefore having girded up the loins of your mind, being sober, hope perfectly upon the grace that is being brought to you in the revelation of Jesus Christ,
texts.1pe.1.14: as obedient children, not fashioning yourselves to the former desires in your ignorance,
texts.1pe.1.15: but according as He who did call you [is] holy, ye also, become holy in all behaviour,
texts.1pe.1.16: because it hath been written, `Become ye holy, because I am holy;'
texts.1pe.1.17: and if on the Father ye do call, who without acceptance of persons is judging according to the work of each, in fear the time of your sojourn pass ye,
texts.1pe.1.18: having known that, not with corruptible things -- silver or gold -- were ye redeemed from your foolish behaviour delivered by fathers,
texts.1pe.1.19: but with precious blood, as of a lamb unblemished and unspotted -- Christ's --
texts.1pe.1.20: foreknown, indeed, before the foundation of the world, and manifested in the last times because of you,
texts.1pe.1.21: who through him do believe in God, who did raise out of the dead, and glory to him did give, so that your faith and hope may be in God.
texts.1pe.1.22: Your souls having purified in the obedience of the truth through the Spirit to brotherly love unfeigned, out of a pure heart one another love ye earnestly,
texts.1pe.1.23: being begotten again, not out of seed corruptible, but incorruptible, through a word of God -- living and remaining -- to the age;
texts.1pe.1.24: because all flesh [is] as grass, and all glory of man as flower of grass; wither did the grass, and the flower of it fell away,
texts.1pe.1.25: and the saying of the Lord doth remain -- to the age; and this is the saying that was proclaimed good news to you.
texts.1pe.2.1: Having put aside, then, all evil, and all guile, and hypocrisies, and envyings, and all evil speakings,
texts.1pe.2.2: as new-born babes the word's pure milk desire ye, that in it ye may grow,
texts.1pe.2.3: if so be ye did taste that the Lord [is] gracious,
texts.1pe.2.4: to whom coming -- a living stone -- by men, indeed, having been disapproved of, but with God choice, precious,
texts.1pe.2.5: and ye yourselves, as living stones, are built up, a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
texts.1pe.2.6: Wherefore, also, it is contained in the Writing: `Lo, I lay in Zion a chief corner-stone, choice, precious, and he who is believing on him may not be put to shame;'
texts.1pe.2.7: to you, then, who are believing [is] the preciousness; and to the unbelieving, a stone that the builders disapproved of, this one did become for the head of a corner,
texts.1pe.2.8: and a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence -- who are stumbling at the word, being unbelieving, -- to which also they were set;
texts.1pe.2.9: and ye [are] a choice race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people acquired, that the excellences ye may shew forth of Him who out of darkness did call you to His wondrous light;
texts.1pe.2.10: who [were] once not a people, and [are] now the people of God; who had not found kindness, and now have found kindness.
texts.1pe.2.11: Beloved, I call upon [you], as strangers and sojourners, to keep from the fleshly desires, that war against the soul,
texts.1pe.2.12: having your behaviour among the nations right, that in that which they speak against you as evil-doers, of the good works having beheld, they may glorify God in a day of inspection.
texts.1pe.2.13: Be subject, then, to every human creation, because of the Lord, whether to a king, as the highest,
texts.1pe.2.14: whether to governors, as to those sent through him, for punishment, indeed, of evil-doers, and a praise of those doing good;
texts.1pe.2.15: because, so is the will of God, doing good, to put to silence the ignorance of the foolish men;
texts.1pe.2.16: as free, and not having the freedom as the cloak of the evil, but as servants of God;
texts.1pe.2.17: to all give ye honour; the brotherhood love ye; God fear ye; the king honour ye.
texts.1pe.2.18: The domestics! be subjecting yourselves in all fear to the masters, not only to the good and gentle, but also to the cross;
texts.1pe.2.19: for this [is] gracious, if because of conscience toward God any one doth endure sorrows, suffering unrighteously;
texts.1pe.2.20: for what renown [is it], if sinning and being buffeted, ye do endure [it]? but if, doing good and suffering [for it], ye do endure, this [is] gracious with God,
texts.1pe.2.21: for to this ye were called, because Christ also did suffer for you, leaving to you an example, that ye may follow his steps,
texts.1pe.2.22: who did not commit sin, nor was guile found in his mouth,
texts.1pe.2.23: who being reviled -- was not reviling again, suffering -- was not threatening, and was committing himself to Him who is judging righteously,
texts.1pe.2.24: who our sins himself did bear in his body, upon the tree, that to the sins having died, to the righteousness we may live; by whose stripes ye were healed,
texts.1pe.2.25: for ye were as sheep going astray, but ye turned back now to the shepherd and overseer of your souls.
texts.1pe.3.1: In like manner, the wives, be ye subject to your own husbands, that even if certain are disobedient to the word, through the conversation of the wives, without the word, they may be won,
texts.1pe.3.2: having beheld your pure behaviour in fear,
texts.1pe.3.3: whose adorning -- let it not be that which is outward, of plaiting of hair, and of putting around of things of gold, or of putting on of garments,
texts.1pe.3.4: but -- the hidden man of the heart, in the incorruptible thing of the meek and quiet spirit, which is, before God, of great price,
texts.1pe.3.5: for thus once also the holy women who did hope on God, were adorning themselves, being subject to their own husbands,
texts.1pe.3.6: as Sarah was obedient to Abraham, calling him `sir,' of whom ye did become daughters, doing good, and not fearing any terror.
texts.1pe.3.7: The husbands, in like manner, dwelling with [them], according to knowledge, as to a weaker vessel -- to the wife -- imparting honour, as also being heirs together of the grace of life, that your prayers be not hindered.
texts.1pe.3.8: And finally, being all of one mind, having fellow-feeling, loving as brethren, compassionate, courteous,
texts.1pe.3.9: not giving back evil for evil, or railing for railing, and on the contrary, blessing, having known that to this ye were called, that a blessing ye may inherit;
texts.1pe.3.10: for `he who is willing to love life, and to see good days, let him guard his tongue from evil, and his lips -- not to speak guile;
texts.1pe.3.11: let him turn aside from evil, and do good, let him seek peace and pursue it;
texts.1pe.3.12: because the eyes of the Lord [are] upon the righteous, and His ears -- to their supplication, and the face of the Lord [is] upon those doing evil;'
texts.1pe.3.13: and who [is] he who will be doing you evil, if of Him who is good ye may become imitators?
texts.1pe.3.14: but if ye also should suffer because of righteousness, happy [are ye]! and of their fear be not afraid, nor be troubled,
texts.1pe.3.15: and the Lord God sanctify in your hearts. And [be] ready always for defence to every one who is asking of you an account concerning the hope that [is] in you, with meekness and fear;
texts.1pe.3.16: having a good conscience, that in that in which they speak against you as evil-doers, they may be ashamed who are traducing your good behaviour in Christ;
texts.1pe.3.17: for [it is] better doing good, if the will of God will it, to suffer, than doing evil;
texts.1pe.3.18: because also Christ once for sin did suffer -- righteous for unrighteous -- that he might lead us to God, having been put to death indeed, in the flesh, and having been made alive in the spirit,
texts.1pe.3.19: in which also to the spirits in prison having gone he did preach,
texts.1pe.3.20: who sometime disbelieved, when once the long-suffering of God did wait, in days of Noah -- an ark being preparing -- in which few, that is, eight souls, were saved through water;
texts.1pe.3.21: also to which an antitype doth now save us -- baptism, (not a putting away of the filth of flesh, but the question of a good conscience in regard to God,) through the rising again of Jesus Christ,
texts.1pe.3.22: who is at the right hand of God, having gone on to heaven -- messengers, and authorities, and powers, having been subjected to him.
texts.1pe.4.1: Christ, then, having suffered for us in the flesh, ye also with the same mind arm yourselves, because he who did suffer in the flesh hath done with sin,
texts.1pe.4.2: no more in the desires of men, but in the will of God, to live the rest of the time in the flesh;
texts.1pe.4.3: for sufficient to us [is] the past time of life the will of the nations to have wrought, having walked in lasciviousnesses, desires, excesses of wines, revelings, drinking-bouts, and unlawful idolatries,
texts.1pe.4.4: in which they think it strange -- your not running with them to the same excess of dissoluteness, speaking evil,
texts.1pe.4.5: who shall give an account to Him who is ready to judge living and dead,
texts.1pe.4.6: for for this also to dead men was good news proclaimed, that they may be judged, indeed, according to men in the flesh, and may live according to God in the spirit.
texts.1pe.4.7: And of all things the end hath come nigh; be sober-minded, then, and watch unto the prayers,
texts.1pe.4.8: and, before all things, to one another having the earnest love, because the love shall cover a multitude of sins;
texts.1pe.4.9: hospitable to one another, without murmuring;
texts.1pe.4.10: each, according as he received a gift, to one another ministering it, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God;
texts.1pe.4.11: if any one doth speak -- `as oracles of God;' if any one doth minister -- `as of the ability which God doth supply;' that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom is the glory and the power -- to the ages of the ages. Amen.
texts.1pe.4.12: Beloved, think it not strange at the fiery suffering among you that is coming to try you, as if a strange thing were happening to you,
texts.1pe.4.13: but, according as ye have fellowship with the sufferings of the Christ, rejoice ye, that also in the revelation of his glory ye may rejoice -- exulting;
texts.1pe.4.14: if ye be reproached in the name of Christ -- happy [are ye], because the Spirit of glory and of God upon you doth rest; in regard, indeed, to them, he is evil-spoken of, and in regard to you, he is glorified;
texts.1pe.4.15: for let none of you suffer as a murderer, or thief, or evil-doer, or as an inspector into other men's matters;
texts.1pe.4.16: and if as a Christian, let him not be ashamed; and let him glorify God in this respect;
texts.1pe.4.17: because it is the time of the beginning of the judgment from the house of God, and if first from us, what the end of those disobedient to the good news of God?
texts.1pe.4.18: And if the righteous man is scarcely saved, the ungodly and sinner -- where shall he appear?
texts.1pe.4.19: so that also those suffering according to the will of god, as to a stedfast Creator, let them commit their own souls in good doing.
texts.1pe.5.1: Elders who [are] among you, I exhort, who [am] a fellow-elder, and a witness of the sufferings of the Christ, and of the glory about to be revealed a partaker,
texts.1pe.5.2: feed the flock of God that [is] among you, overseeing not constrainedly, but willingly, neither for filthy lucre, but of a ready mind,
texts.1pe.5.3: neither as exercising lordship over the heritages, but patterns becoming of the flock,
texts.1pe.5.4: and at the manifestation of the chief Shepherd, ye shall receive the unfading crown of glory.
texts.1pe.5.5: In like manner, ye younger, be subject to elders, and all to one another subjecting yourselves; with humble-mindedness clothe yourselves, because God the proud doth resist, but to the humble He doth give grace;
texts.1pe.5.6: be humbled, then, under the powerful hand of God, that you He may exalt in good time,
texts.1pe.5.7: all your care having cast upon Him, because He careth for you.
texts.1pe.5.8: Be sober, vigilant, because your opponent the devil, as a roaring lion, doth walk about, seeking whom he may swallow up,
texts.1pe.5.9: whom resist, stedfast in the faith, having known the same sufferings to your brotherhood in the world to be accomplished.
texts.1pe.5.10: And the God of all grace, who did call you to His age-during glory in Christ Jesus, having suffered a little, Himself make you perfect, establish, strengthen, settle [you];
texts.1pe.5.11: to Him [is] the glory, and the power -- to the ages and the ages! Amen.
texts.1pe.5.12: Through Silvanus, to you the faithful brother, as I reckon, through few [words] I did write, exhorting and testifying this to be the true grace of God in which ye have stood.
texts.1pe.5.13: Salute you doth the [assembly] in Babylon jointly elected, and Markus my son.
texts.1pe.5.14: Salute ye one another in a kiss of love; peace to you all who [are] in Christ Jesus! Amen.

texts.1pe.1.1: Pedro, apóstol de Jesu Cristo, a los extranjeros que están esparcidos en Ponto, en Galacia, en Capadocia, en Asia, y en Bitinia:
texts.1pe.1.2: Elegidos según la presciencia de Dios el Padre, en santificación del Espíritu, para obedecer, y ser rociados con la sangre de Jesu Cristo: Gracia y paz os sea multiplicada.
texts.1pe.1.3: Alabado sea el Dios y Padre de nuestro Señor Jesu Cristo, el cual según su grande misericordia nos ha reengendrado en esperanza viva, por la resurrección de Jesu Cristo de entre los muertos;
texts.1pe.1.4: Para la herencia incorruptible, y que no puede contaminarse, ni marchitarse, conservada en los cielos para vosotros,
texts.1pe.1.5: Que sois guardados en la virtud de Dios por medio de la fe, para alcanzar la salvación que está aparejada para ser manifestada en el postrimero tiempo.
texts.1pe.1.6: En lo cual vosotros os regocijáis grandemente, estando al presente un poco de tiempo, si es necesario, afligidos en diversas tentaciones.
texts.1pe.1.7: Para que la prueba de vuestra fe, muy más preciosa que el oro, (el cual perece, mas empero es probado con fuego,) sea hallada en alabanza, y gloria, y honra, cuando Jesu Cristo fuere manifestado:
texts.1pe.1.8: Al cual no habiendo visto, le amáis: en el cual creyendo, aunque al presente no le veais, os alegráis con gozo inefable y lleno de gloria;
texts.1pe.1.9: Recibiendo el fin de vuestra fe, que es, la salud de vuestras almas.
texts.1pe.1.10: De la cual salud los profetas (que profetizaron de la gracia que había de venir en vosotros) han inquirido, y diligentemente buscado:
texts.1pe.1.11: Escudriñando cuándo, y en qué punto de tiempo significaba el Espíritu de Cristo que estaba en ellos: el cual antes anunciaba las aflicciones que habían de venir a Cristo, y las glorias después de ellas:
texts.1pe.1.12: A los cuales fue revelado, que no para sí mismos, sino para nosotros administraban las cosas, que ahora os son anunciadas de los que os han predicado el evangelio, por el Espíritu Santo enviado del cielo: en las cuales cosas desean mirar los ángeles.
texts.1pe.1.13: Por lo cual teniendo los lomos de vuestro entendimiento ceñidos, y sobrios, esperád perfectamente en la gracia que se os ha de traer en la manifestación de Jesu Cristo:
texts.1pe.1.14: Como hijos obedientes, no conformándoos con las concupiscencias que antes teníais estando en vuestra ignorancia;
texts.1pe.1.15: Mas como aquel que os ha llamado es santo, semejantemente también vosotros sed santos en todo proceder;
texts.1pe.1.16: Porque escrito está: Sed santos, porque yo soy santo.
texts.1pe.1.17: Y si invocáis por Padre a aquel que sin acepción de personas juzga según la obra de cada uno, conversád en temor todo el tiempo de vuestra peregrinación:
texts.1pe.1.18: Sabiendo que habéis sido rescatados de vuestra vana conversación, (la cual recibisteis de vuestros padres,) no con cosas corruptibles, como oro o plata;
texts.1pe.1.19: Mas con la sangre preciosa de Cristo, como de un cordero sin mancha, y sin contaminación:
texts.1pe.1.20: Ya preordinado ciertamente de antes de la fundación del mundo, pero manifestado en los postrimeros tiempos por amor de vosotros,
texts.1pe.1.21: Que por medio de él creeis en Dios, el cual le resucitó de entre los muertos, y le ha dado gloria, para que vuestra fe y esperanza sea en Dios:
texts.1pe.1.22: Habiendo purificado vuestras almas en la obediencia de la verdad, por medio del Espíritu, para un amor hermanable, sin fingimiento amáos unos a otros entrañablemente de corazón puro:
texts.1pe.1.23: Siendo renacidos, no de simiente corruptible, sino de incorruptible, por la palabra del Dios viviente, y que permanece para siempre.
texts.1pe.1.24: Porque toda carne es como yerba, y toda la gloria del hombre como la flor de la yerba: la yerba se secó, y la flor se cayó;
texts.1pe.1.25: Mas la palabra del Señor permanece perpetuamente: y esta es la palabra que por el evangelio os ha sido evangelizada.
texts.1pe.2.1: Por lo que desechando toda malicia, y todo engaño, y fingimientos, y envidias, y toda habla mala,
texts.1pe.2.2: Como niños recién nacidos, deseád ardientemente la leche no adulterada de la palabra, para que por ella crezcáis:
texts.1pe.2.3: Si empero habéis gustado que el Señor es benigno.
texts.1pe.2.4: Al cual allegándoos, como a la piedra viva, reprobada cierto de los hombres, empero elegida de Dios, y preciosa,
texts.1pe.2.5: Vosotros también, como piedras vivas, sed edificados para ser una casa espiritual, un sacerdocio santo, para ofrecer sacrificios espirituales, agradables a Dios por medio de Jesu Cristo.
texts.1pe.2.6: Por lo cual también contiene la Escritura: He aquí, yo pongo en Sión la principal piedra del ángulo, escogida, preciosa; y el que creyere en él no será confundido.
texts.1pe.2.7: Para vosotros pues que creeis él es precioso; mas para los desobedientes, la piedra que los edificadores reprobaron, esta fue hecha la cabeza del ángulo,
texts.1pe.2.8: Y piedra de tropiezo, y roca de escándalo, a aquellos que tropiezan en la palabra, siendo desobedientes; a lo que también fueron destinados.
texts.1pe.2.9: Mas vosotros sois el linaje elegido, el real sacerdocio, nación santa, pueblo ganado, para que anuncieis las virtudes de aquel que os ha llamado de las tinieblas a su luz admirable:
texts.1pe.2.10: Vosotros, que en el tiempo pasado eráis no pueblo, mas ahora sois pueblo de Dios, que en el tiempo pasado no habíais alcanzado misericordia, mas ahora habéis ya alcanzado misericordia.
texts.1pe.2.11: Amados, yo os ruego, como a extranjeros y caminantes, os abstengáis de los deseos carnales, que batallan contra el alma,
texts.1pe.2.12: Y tengáis vuestra conversación honesta entre los Gentiles; para que en lo que ellos murmuran de vosotros como de malhechores, glorifiquen a Dios en el día de la visitación, estimándoos por las buenas obras.
texts.1pe.2.13: Sed pues sujetos a toda ordenación humana por causa del Señor: ahora sea a rey, como a superior:
texts.1pe.2.14: Ahora a los gobernadores, como enviados por él, para venganza de los malhechores, y para loor de los que hacen bien.
texts.1pe.2.15: Porque esta es la voluntad de Dios, que haciendo bien, embozaléis la ignorancia de los hombres vanos:
texts.1pe.2.16: Como estando en libertad, y no como teniendo la libertad por cobertura de malicia, sino como siervos de Dios.
texts.1pe.2.17: Honrád a todos. Amád la fraternidad. Teméd a Dios. Honrád al rey.
texts.1pe.2.18: Vosotros, siervos, sed sujetos con todo temor a vuestros señores; no solamente a los buenos y humanos, mas aun también a los rigurosos.
texts.1pe.2.19: Porque esto es agradable, si alguno a causa de la conciencia, que tiene delante de Dios, sufre molestias, padeciendo injustamente.
texts.1pe.2.20: Porque ¿qué gloria es, si pecando vosotros sois abofeteados, y lo sufrís? empero si haciendo bien, sois afligidos, y lo sufrís, esto es cierto agradable delante de Dios.
texts.1pe.2.21: Porque para esto fuisteis llamados, pues que también Cristo padeció por nosotros, dejándonos un modelo, para que vosotros sigáis sus pisadas.
texts.1pe.2.22: El cual no hizo pecado, ni fue hallado engaño en su boca:
texts.1pe.2.23: El cual maldiciéndole, no tornaba a maldecir; y cuando padecía, no amenazaba; sino que remitía su causa al que juzga justamente.
texts.1pe.2.24: El mismo que llevó nuestros pecados en su cuerpo sobre el madero, para que nosotros siendo muertos a los pecados, viviésemos a la justicia. Por las heridas del cual habéis sido sanados.
texts.1pe.2.25: Porque vosotros eráis como ovejas descarriadas; mas ahora sois ya convertidos al Pastor, y Obispo de vuestras almas.
texts.1pe.3.1: Semejantemente vosotras mujeres, sed sujetas a vuestros maridos; para que si también algunos no creen a la palabra, sean ganados sin palabra por la conversación de las mujeres:
texts.1pe.3.2: Considerando vuestra casta conversación, que es con reverencia.
texts.1pe.3.3: La compostura de las cuales, no sea exterior con encrespamiento de cabellos, y atavío de oro, ni en composición de ropas;
texts.1pe.3.4: Mas el hombre del corazón que está encubierto sea sin toda corrupción, y de espíritu agradable, y pacífico, lo cual es de grande estima delante de Dios.
texts.1pe.3.5: Porque así también se ataviaban en el tiempo antiguo aquellas santas mujeres que esperaban en Dios, estando sujetas a sus propios maridos:
texts.1pe.3.6: Al modo que Sara obedecía a Abraham, llamándole señor: de la cual vosotras sois hechas hijas, haciendo bien, y no siendo amedrentadas de ningún pavor.
texts.1pe.3.7: Vosotros maridos semejantemente cohabitád con ellas según ciencia, dando honor a la mujer, como a vaso más frágil, y como a herederas juntamente de la gracia de vida; para que vuestras oraciones no sean impedidas.
texts.1pe.3.8: Y finalmente sed todos de un consentimiento, de una afección, amándoos hermanablemente, misericordiosos, amigables,
texts.1pe.3.9: No volviendo mal por mal, ni maldición por maldición, sino antes por el contrario, bendiciendo: sabiendo que para esto vosotros fuisteis llamados, para que poseáis en herencia bendición.
texts.1pe.3.10: Porque el que quiere amar la vida, y ver los días buenos, refrene su lengua de mal, y sus labios no hablen engaño.
texts.1pe.3.11: Apártese del mal, y haga bien: busque la paz, y sígala.
texts.1pe.3.12: Porque los ojos del Señor están sobre los justos, y sus oídos atentos a sus oraciones: el rostro del Señor está sobre aquellos que hacen mal.
texts.1pe.3.13: ¿Y quién es aquel que os podrá empecer, si fueseis imitadores del bueno?
texts.1pe.3.14: Mas también si alguna cosa padecéis por amor a la justicia, sois bienaventurados. Por tanto no temáis por el temor de aquellos, y no seáis turbados;
texts.1pe.3.15: Mas santificád al Señor Dios en vuestros corazones; y estád siempre aparejados para responder a cada uno que os demanda razón de la esperanza que está en vosotros; y esto con mansedumbre y reverencia;
texts.1pe.3.16: Teniendo buena conciencia, para que en lo que dicen mal de vosotros como de malhechores, sean confundidos los que calumnian vuestro buen proceder en Cristo.
texts.1pe.3.17: Porque mejor es que padezcáis haciendo bien, (si la voluntad de Dios así lo quiere,) que no haciendo mal.
texts.1pe.3.18: Porque también Cristo padeció una vez por los pecados, el justo por los injustos, para llevarnos a Dios, mortificado a la verdad en la carne, pero vivificado por el Espíritu.
texts.1pe.3.19: En el cual también fue, y predicó a los espíritus que estaban en cárcel:
texts.1pe.3.20: Los cuales en el tiempo pasado fueron desobedientes, cuando una vez se esperaba la paciencia de Dios, en los días de Noé, cuando se aparejaba el arca, en la cual pocas, es a saber, ocho personas, fueron salvas por agua.
texts.1pe.3.21: A la figura de la cual el bautismo, que ahora corresponde, nos salva a nosotros también, (no quitando las inmundicias de la carne, mas dando testimonio de buena conciencia delante de Dios,) por medio de la resurrección de Jesu Cristo:
texts.1pe.3.22: El cual, siendo subido al cielo, está a la diestra de Dios: a quien están sujetos los ángeles, y las potestades, y virtudes.
texts.1pe.4.1: Pues que Cristo ha padecido por nosotros en la carne, vosotros también estád armados del mismo pensamiento: que el que ha padecido en la carne, cesó de pecado;
texts.1pe.4.2: Para que ya el tiempo que queda en carne, viva, no a las concupiscencias de los hombres, sino a la voluntad de Dios.
texts.1pe.4.3: Porque nos debe bastar que el tiempo pasado de nuestra vida hayamos hecho la voluntad de los Gentiles, cuando conversábamos en lujurias, en concupiscencias, en embriagueces, en glotonerías, en beberes, y en abominables idolatrías.
texts.1pe.4.4: En lo cual les parece cosa extraña de que vosotros no corráis juntamente con ellos en el mismo desenfrenamiento de disolución, ultrajándo os:
texts.1pe.4.5: Los cuales darán cuenta al que está aparejado para juzgar los vivos y los muertos.
texts.1pe.4.6: Porque por esto ha sido predicado también el evangelio a los muertos; para que sean juzgados según los hombres en la carne, mas vivan según Dios en el espíritu.
texts.1pe.4.7: Mas el fin de todas las cosas se acerca. Sed pues templados, y velád en oración.
texts.1pe.4.8: Y sobre todo tenéd entre vosotros ferviente caridad; porque la caridad cubrirá la multitud de pecados.
texts.1pe.4.9: Hospedáos amorosamente los unos a los otros sin murmuraciones.
texts.1pe.4.10: Cada uno según el don que ha recibido, adminístrelo a los otros, como buenos dispensadores de las diferentes gracias de Dios.
texts.1pe.4.11: Si alguno habla, hable conforme a los oráculos de Dios: si alguno ministra, ministre conforme a la virtud que Dios da: para que en todas cosas sea Dios glorificado por medio de Jesu Cristo, al cual es gloria, e imperio para siempre jamás. Amén.
texts.1pe.4.12: Carísimos, no os maravilléis cuando sois examinados por fuego, (lo cual se hace para vuestra prueba,) como si alguna cosa peregrina os aconteciese;
texts.1pe.4.13: Mas antes, en que sois participantes de las aflicciones de Cristo, regocijáos; para que también en la revelación de su gloria os regocijéis saltando de gozo.
texts.1pe.4.14: Si sois vituperados por el nombre de Cristo, sois bienaventurados; porque el Espíritu de gloria, y de Dios reposa sobre vosotros. Cierto según ellos él es blasfemado, mas según vosotros es glorificado.
texts.1pe.4.15: Así que no sea ninguno de vosotros afligido como homicida, o ladrón, o malhechor, o explorador de lo ajeno.
texts.1pe.4.16: Pero si alguno es afligido como Cristiano, no se avergüence, antes glorifique a Dios en esta parte.
texts.1pe.4.17: Porque ya es tiempo que el juicio comience por la casa de Dios; y si primero comienza por nosotros, ¿qué fin será el de aquellos que no obedecen al evangelio de Dios?
texts.1pe.4.18: Y si el justo es dificultosamente salvo, ¿adónde parecerá el infiel, y el pecador?
texts.1pe.4.19: Por lo que, aun los que son afligidos según la voluntad de Dios, encomiénden le sus almas, haciendo bien, como a su fiel Creador.
texts.1pe.5.1: Yo ruego a los ancianos que están entre vosotros, (yo anciano también con ellos, y testigo de las aflicciones de Cristo, que soy también participante de la gloria que ha de ser revelada:)
texts.1pe.5.2: Apacentád el rebaño de Dios que está ent re vosotros, teniendo cuidado de él, no por fuerza, mas voluntariamente: no por ganancia deshonesta, sino de un ánimo pronto;
texts.1pe.5.3: Y no como teniendo señorío sobre las herencias de Dios, sino de tal manera que seáis dechados de la grey.
texts.1pe.5.4: Y cuando apareciere el Príncipe de los pastores, vosotros recibiréis la corona inmarcesible de gloria.
texts.1pe.5.5: Semejantemente vosotros los jóvenes, sed sujetos a los ancianos, de tal manera que seáis todos sujetos uno a otro. Vestíos de humildad de ánimo; porque Dios resiste a los soberbios, y da gracia a los humildes.
texts.1pe.5.6: Humilláos pues debajo de la poderosa mano de Dios, para que él os ensalce cuando fuere tiempo:
texts.1pe.5.7: Echando toda vuestra solicitud en él; porque él tiene cuidado de vosotros.
texts.1pe.5.8: Sed templados, y velád; porque vuestro adversario el diablo anda como león bramando en derredor de vosotros, buscando alguno que trague:
texts.1pe.5.9: Al cual resistíd firmes en la fe, sabiendo que las mismas aflicciones han de ser cumplidas en la compañía de vuestros hermanos que están en el mundo.
texts.1pe.5.10: Mas el Dios de toda gracia, que nos ha llamado a su gloria eterna por Jesu Cristo, después que hubiereis un poco de tiempo padecido, el mismo os perfeccione, confirme, corrobore, y establezca:
texts.1pe.5.11: A él la gloria, y el imperio para siempre. Amén.
texts.1pe.5.12: Por Silvano que os es (según yo pienso) hermano fiel, os he escrito brevemente, amonestándoos, y testificándo os, que ésta es la verdadera gracia de Dios, en la cual estáis.
texts.1pe.5.13: La iglesia que está en Babilonia, juntamente elegida con vosotros, se os encomienda, y Márcos mi hijo.
texts.1pe.5.14: Saludáos unos a otros con beso de amor. Paz a vosotros todos, los que estáis en Cristo Jesús. Amén.

texts.1pe.1.1: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, unto the chosen pilgrims of the dispersion, throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia,—
texts.1pe.1.2: [Chosen] according to the fore-knowledge of God the Father, in sanctification of Spirit, unto obedience and the sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ, Favour unto you, and peace, be multiplied!
texts.1pe.1.3: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, Who, according to his great mercy, hath regenerated us unto a living hope, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from among the dead,
texts.1pe.1.4: Unto an inheritance, incorruptible and undefiled and unfading, reserved in the heavens for you
texts.1pe.1.5: who, in God’s power, are being guarded through faith unto salvation—ready to be revealed in the last ripe time:
texts.1pe.1.6: Wherein ye exult, though, for a little, just now, if needful, put to grief in manifold temptations,
texts.1pe.1.7: In order that the proving of your faith—much more precious than of gold that perisheth even though, by means of fire, it is proved—may be found unto praise and glory and honour in the revealing of Jesus Christ,—
texts.1pe.1.8: Whom, not having seen, ye love, on whom, though at present not looking, but believing, ye exult with joy unspeakable and filled with glory,
texts.1pe.1.9: Being about to bear away the end of your faith—a salvation of souls:
texts.1pe.1.10: Concerning which salvation, prophets—who concerning the favour for you, did prophesy—sought out and searched out,
texts.1pe.1.11: Searching into what particular, or what manner, of season the Spirit of Christ which was in them was pointing to, when witnessing beforehand as to—The sufferings, for Christ, and the glories, after these,—
texts.1pe.1.12: Unto whom it was revealed—that, Not unto themselves, but unto us, they were ministering them, which things have, now, been announced unto you through them who have told you the good tidings with Holy Spirit sent forth from heaven: into which things messengers are coveting to obtain a nearer view.
texts.1pe.1.13: Wherefore, girding up the loins of your mind, keeping sober, perseveringly direct your hope unto the favour, being borne along to you, in the revealing of Jesus Christ:
texts.1pe.1.14: As obedient persons, not configuring yourselves unto your former covetings in your ignorance:
texts.1pe.1.15: But, according as he that hath called you is holy, do, ye yourselves, also become, holy in all manner of behaviour,—
texts.1pe.1.16: Inasmuch as it is written—Holy shall ye be, because, I, am holy.
texts.1pe.1.17: And, if, as Father, ye are invoking him who, without respect of persons, judgeth according to each man’s work, with reverence, for the time of your sojourning, behave ye;
texts.1pe.1.18: Knowing that, Not with corruptible things, with silver or gold, have ye been redeemed from your unmeaning behaviour paternally handed down,
texts.1pe.1.19: But with precious blood, as of a lamb, unblemished and unspotted, of an Anointed One,—
texts.1pe.1.20: Foreknown, indeed, before the foundation of the world, but made manifest at a last stage of the times, for the sake of you
texts.1pe.1.21: who, through him, are faithful towards God,—Who raised him from among the dead, and glory to him gave, So that your faith and hope are directed towards God:
texts.1pe.1.22: Having purified, your souls, by the obedience of the truth, unto unfeigned brotherly affection, from the heart, love, one another, earnestly;
texts.1pe.1.23: Having been regenerated—Not out of corruptible seed, but incorruptible—through means of the word of a Living and Abiding God;
texts.1pe.1.24: Inasmuch as—All flesh, is as grass, and, all the glory thereof, as the flower of grass,—The grass hath withered, and the flower hath fallen out,
texts.1pe.1.25: But the declaration of the Lord age-abidingly remaineth; And, this, is a declaration which in the joyful message hath been announced unto you.
texts.1pe.2.1: Putting away, therefore, all vice and all deceit and hypocrisy and envyings and all detractions,
texts.1pe.2.2: As new-born babes, for the pure milk that is for the mind, eagerly crave, that, thereby, ye may grow unto salvation:—
texts.1pe.2.3: If ye have tasted for yourselves that, gracious, is the Lord,—
texts.1pe.2.4: Unto whom coming near, as unto a living stone—by men, indeed, rejected, but, with God, chosen, held in honour,
texts.1pe.2.5: Yourselves also, as living stones, are being built up a spiritual house, for a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices, well-pleasing unto God through Jesus Christ;
texts.1pe.2.6: Inasmuch as it is contained in scripture—Lo! I lay in Zion an outmost corner stone, chosen, held in honour, and, he that resteth faith thereupon, shall not be put to shame.
texts.1pe.2.7: Unto you, then, is the honour—[unto you] who believe; but, unto such as disbelieve, The stone which the builders rejected,—The same, hath become head of the corner,
texts.1pe.2.8: And a stone to strike against, and a rock to stumble over: Who stumble because, unto the word, they do not yield,—unto which also they have been appointed;
texts.1pe.2.9: But, ye, are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for a peculiar treasure, that, the excellences, ye may tell forth, of him who, out of darkness, hath called you into his marvellous light:—
texts.1pe.2.10: Who, at one time, were a No-people, but, now, are a people of God,—who had not been enjoying mercy, but, now, have received mercy.
texts.1pe.2.11: Beloved! I exhort you, as sojourners and pilgrims, to abstain from fleshly covetings, such as take the field against the soul;
texts.1pe.2.12: Having, your behaviour among the nations, honourable,—in order that, wherein they speak against you as evil-doers, they may, owing to the honourable works they are permitted to behold, glorify God in the day of visitation.
texts.1pe.2.13: Submit yourselves unto every human creation, for the Lord’s sake,—whether unto a king, as one that protecteth,
texts.1pe.2.14: Or unto governors, as, through him, sent—for vengeance on evil-doers, but praise to such as do good;
texts.1pe.2.15: Because, so, is the will of God,—by doing good, to be putting to silence, the ignorance of heedless men:
texts.1pe.2.16: As free, yet, not as a cloak of vice, holding your freedom, but, as God’s servants.
texts.1pe.2.17: Unto all men, give honour, unto the brotherhood, shew love, unto God, give reverence, the king, hold in honour.
texts.1pe.2.18: Ye domestics, submitting yourselves, in all reverence, unto your masters,—not only unto the good and considerate, but also unto the perverse;
texts.1pe.2.19: For, this, is thankworthy,—If, for the sake of conscience towards God, one beareth griefs, suffering wrongfully,—
texts.1pe.2.20: For what sort of honour is it—if, committing sin, and being buffeted, ye endure it? But, if, doing good, and suffering, ye endure it, this, is thankworthy with God.
texts.1pe.2.21: For, hereunto, have ye been called; because, Christ also, suffered in your behalf, unto you, leaving behind a pattern, that ye might follow in his steps:
texts.1pe.2.22: Who did not, a sin, commit, neither was deceit found in his mouth,—
texts.1pe.2.23: Who, being reviled, was not reviling again, suffering, he was not threatening, but was making surrender unto him that judgeth righteously,—
texts.1pe.2.24: Who, our sins, himself, bare up, in his body, unto the tree, in order that we, from our sins getting away, in righteousness, might live,—by whose stripes, ye have been healed;
texts.1pe.2.25: For ye were as sheep going astray, but have now turned back unto the shepherd and overseer of your souls.
texts.1pe.3.1: In like manner, ye wives,—submitting yourselves unto your own husbands; in order that, if any are not yielding unto the word, through their wives behaviour, they may, without the word, be won,
texts.1pe.3.2: Having been permitted to behold your reverently chaste behaviour,—
texts.1pe.3.3: Whose adorning, let it be—not the outward, of plaiting the hair and wearing golden ornaments, or putting on of apparel,
texts.1pe.3.4: But the hidden character, of the heart,—in the incorruptible [ornament] of the quiet, and meek, spirit, which is, in presence of God, of great price.
texts.1pe.3.5: For, so, at one time, the holy women also, who directed their hope towards God, used to adorn themselves, being in submission unto their own husbands:
texts.1pe.3.6: As, Sarah, was obedient unto Abraham, calling him, lord,—whose children ye have become—so long as ye are doing good, and not bringing yourselves into fear of any single cause of alarm.
texts.1pe.3.7: Ye husbands, in like manner, dwelling with them according to knowledge,—as unto a weaker vessel, unto the female [vessel], assigning honour, as joint—inheritors also of life’s favour,—to the end that unhindered may be, your prayers.
texts.1pe.3.8: And, finally, all, being of one mind, having fellow—feeling, attached to the brethren, of tender affection, of lowly mind:
texts.1pe.3.9: Not returning evil for evil, nor reviling for reviling, but, on the contrary, bestowing a blessing,—because, hereunto, have ye been called, in order that, a blessing, ye might inherit.
